title: kv-cache: adaptive memory eviction + spillover + defrag heuristics v17
author: Emily Chen
description: Motivation: production hosts with mixed-length workloads observed increased KV cache fragmentation and thrashing when memory pressure caused spillover to host paging; this led to higher tail latency and increased GPU memory churn during continuous batching. This PR implements an adaptive memory management pipeline for the KV cache that combines: 1) a soft/hard memory threshold model with hysteresis to avoid oscillation, 2) prioritized spillover to host with eviction preference for cold fragmented slabs, 3) background defragmentation and compaction heuristics that operate per-model and per-device to reduce fragmentation without impacting critical request latency, and 4) hot-entry pinning and request-aware reservation so active sequences avoid eviction while being served by continuous batching. Key behaviors: - soft_threshold_pct and hard_threshold_pct tunables with default 0.75/0.9, configurable per-pool and per-model. - spillover_mode supports 'host-page' and 'disk-async' with staged fallback. Host-page moves least-recent and largest-fragment entries first. - defrag runs as low-priority background jobs that prefer idle GPUs; loopback to scheduler ensures compaction jobs yield to latency-critical qps traffic. - adaptive eviction scoring that combines LRU recency, fragment size, estimated rehydrate cost, and request hit-rate to avoid evicting frequently reaccessed KV slices. - continuous-batching integration: batches now expose in-flight KV pin tokens to the eviction controller so active KVs are temporarily protected. - telemetry: new metrics kvcache.memory_used_pct, kvcache.fragmentation_ratio, kvcache.spillover_rate, kvcache.defrag_jobs_{scheduled,completed,failed}, and per-model kvcache.hot_entry_hits. Implementation summary: - core runtime changes in src/runtime/kv_cache_manager.cc/.h: new memory accounting, eviction scorer, and defrag job queue. - scheduler hooks added in src/runtime/scheduler.cc to pause/resume defrag jobs and to enable request-aware reservations. - host spillover implemented in src/platform/host_spillover.{cc,h} with an async page writer and eviction shadow index. - config surface in config/kvcache.yaml and runtime flags in include/runtime/flags.h. - unit and integration tests in tests/kv_cache/* and an e2e perf canary in perf/kvcache_canary. Compatibility and safety: defaults preserve current behavior when feature flag kvcache.adaptive_eviction is off. We added conservative rollout gates and a canary routine that runs on 5% of capacity for 72h before org-wide rollout. Performance: microbenchmarks show 8-12% lower mean tail GPU memory churn and 15-25% reduction in 99th token latency for mixed short/long workloads vs baseline on p4d-like infra. Observability: dashboards added to grafana/dashboards/kv_cache_memory.json and alerting thresholds to prometheus/alerts/kvcache_alerts.yaml. Testing: extensive unit tests + integration against the canary cluster. Migration notes: cluster operators should tune soft/hard thresholds based on workload profile and enable host-page spillover only when host memory margins allow. Rollback: feature flag and cluster-wide kill-switch included. Related: builds on prior spillover/defrag efforts (see ENG-1432 series) and addresses regressions observed in SUP-8123.
